To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dietary inclusion of rie, a model ingredient for increased gut viscosity, had limited effects on growth performance of broilers, but did affect gut morphology, microbiome composition and gene expression profiles in the jejunum.

inclusion of rye to the diet of broilers between 14 and d 28 of age had no effects on performance, but affected the gut wall morphology and the expression of genes involved with the immune competence in the jejunal tissue.

dietary inclusion of ryesupplementation to broiler diets affects immune competence of broilers, as evidenced by altered expression of genes related to cell cycle processes in the gut wall, altered microbiota composition in jejunal digesta and altered morphology of the small intestine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of rye inclusion to improve gut health and immunity of broilers, and the underlying mechanisms.
the effects of dietary rye on immune competence‐ and performance‐related parameters in broilers.
the potential of dietary rye inclusion to affect immune competence‐related traits in broilers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune competence of the broilers was affected by dietary inclusion level of rye, but this effect was not related to changes in immune competence‐related performance parameters.

dietary rye inclusion between 14 and d 28 d of broilers had a limited effect on immune competence, and that further research is required to elucidate its effect on immune competence in broiler chickens.
dietary rye inclusion levels between 5% and 10% in broiler diets have a limited negative impact on performance of broilers, but might have a positive impact on the gut health of these animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rye inclusion in broiler diets may affect immune competence of birds, which might be related to the increased viscosity of the digesta.
rye inclusion in broiler grower diets may not affect the performance but may affect the immune competence of broilers.
rye inclusion in broiler diets may affect immune competence of broiler birds, which in turn may affect their performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of rye in broiler diets can be used as a tool to study the effects of dietary viscosity on immune competence of broilers.
rye inclusion in the diet of broilers may have effects on gut health and immune competence, but these effects are limited.
